comparison: Both strongly support the age-related increase in rG4 staining in the hippocampus (C37-C41). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis (Spearman R=0.49, p=0.038 in OML) and notes regional specificity, while peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'compelling' and methods as 'robust and reproducible.' Complete agreement on this finding.

Both strongly support the correlation between BG4 staining and Alzheimer's disease severity/Braak stage (C42-C44). OpenEval details the statistical significance and regional specificity, while all three peer reviewers explicitly confirm this as 'compelling evidence.' Complete agreement on this correlation.

Both support the association between APOE4 genotype and increased rG4 staining (C47, C59, C82). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes limitations regarding small sample size and population stratification. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the finding without raising these concerns. Agreement on the finding, but OpenEval more cautious about generalizability.

Both support the co-localization of BG4 with phosphorylated tau (C53-C55). OpenEval provides quantitative details (82-85% of p-Tau-positive cells contain BG4) and notes the directionality caveat. Peer reviewers confirm the co-localization without discussing directionality. Agreement on the observation.

Both support the validation of BG4 staining specificity through rRNA co-localization (C48-C50). OpenEval explicitly discusses the methodological rationale and potential DNA staining caveat. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the validation by describing methods as 'robust and reproducible' without challenging specificity. Agreement on validation approach.

Both support the cell-type distribution findings (C51-C52). OpenEval details co-staining with neuronal, oligodendrocyte, and astrocyte markers but not microglial markers. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the overall 'robust and reproducible' methodology. Complete agreement.

Both support the CD spectroscopy evidence for parallel rG4 structure formation (C34, C85). OpenEval provides detailed structural interpretation of the CD spectrum. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this biophysical characterization without challenge. Agreement on structural validation.

Major disagreement on the mechanistic model (C7, C61-C63, C76). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is speculative, based on correlative evidence, and lacks direct mechanistic testing. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 calling it 'interesting' and the editor describing results as 'fundamental' that 'will rejuvenate understanding.' Significant divergence in evaluation.

Disagreement on translational applications (C69-C70). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting therapeutic and diagnostic potential remains speculative without demonstration of disease modulation or biomarker accessibility. Peer reviewers implicitly support the translational potential through the editor's statement about 'fundamental' results. Divergence in assessment of translational claims.

Both support the novelty claims (C2, C35). OpenEval notes the systematic examination of rG4 in human brain tissue appears novel. Reviewer 1 explicitly confirms 'this is the first time that BG4 staining is used in this context.' Complete agreement on novelty.

OpenEval rates the causal claim that 'rG4 structure can drive tau aggregation' (C5, C33-C34) as UNCERTAIN, noting it combines current CD data with previous cellular studies without direct mechanistic testing in this manuscript. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this causal claim distinction.

OpenEval supports the study design and methodology description (C36, C77-C79), noting appropriate sample characteristics, antibody validation, and standard neuropathological methods. Peer reviewers make general statements about 'robust and reproducible' methods but do not provide a separate evaluation specifically focused on methodological claims.

OpenEval supports the extensive background and literature context claims (C1, C8-C32, C45-C46, C60, C64, C67-C68, C72-C75, C80-C81) as appropriately cited. Peer reviewers do not provide separate evaluation of background/contextual claims.

OpenEval rates speculative alternative mechanisms (C66) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting it is presented as speculation for future investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this specific speculative claim.
